visual.general_description: Composite laboratory photograph of column agglutination (gel card) tests: an upper card labeled "Antibody screen" and three lower cards labeled "Antibody identification".
visual.detailed_description: Upper image: one gel card with six microtubes; the first three have handwritten roman numerals I, II and III above a printed AHG strip. In the first tube a red cell pellet sits at the bottom with an otherwise clear gel; in the second and third tubes red cell clumps are scattered through the upper-middle gel with a small pellet at the bottom. The fourth to sixth tubes show only pale teal liquid with no red cells. A black rectangle covers part of the card label area and a white text box with the printed words "Antibody screen" overlies the lower left. Lower image: three side-by-side gel cards in a strip headed by a white text box with the printed words "Antibody identification". Handwritten numbers 1 to 6 (numerals 2 and 3 overwritten) mark the first card, 7 to 12 the second and 13 to 16 the third, whose last two tubes are unnumbered and contain only teal liquid. Each numbered tube has a red cell pellet at the bottom; in several tubes (including 1, 3, 4, 7, 9, 11, 14 and 16) additional red cells are scattered above the pellet within the gel, and others show a compact pellet with clear gel. Black rectangles cover parts of the label areas of all three lower cards. No axes, numeric readings, arrows or panel letters are printed.
